BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI  ON THE 12th OF MARCH, 2025  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 11058 of 2025  UDEY SINGH  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH  Appearance:
 Shri Laveesh Sethia - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Kshitij Vyas - Panel Lawyer for the respondent /
 ORDER

This first bail application under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha 2023 (equivalent to Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the applicant Udey Singh S/o Gangaram Tanwar for grant of regular bail, who has been arrested on 18/02/2025 in connection with Crime No.241/2024 registered at Police Station Agar, District Agar Malwa (M.P.) for commission of offences under Sections 363, 366, 368, 376 and 376(2)(n) of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 3/4 and 5(L)/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the crime.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: There is no sufficient evidence available on record to establish the complicity of the accused with the alleged crime.
Main accused is the son of the applicant Laxman.
The only allegation against the applicant is that he has given shelter to his son in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6742 2 MCRC-11058-2025 his house.
Victim remained with the co-accused Laxman for near about eight months.
As per prosecution case, age of the victim is 17 years.
Investigation is about to complete and therefore, no further custodial interrogation of the applicant is required.
He is in jail sine 18/02/2025 and will abide by all the terms and conditions imposed by this Court.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family, home and profession and also there is no likelihood of tampering with evidence by applicant.
Final conclusion of the trial will take considerable long time, therefore, learned counsel prays for allowing the bail application and for grant of bail.

3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State has vehemently opposed the prayer and prays for dismissal of the bail application but fairly admits that no allegation regarding sexual assault is on the applicant but opposed the prayer on the ground that applicant has given shelter to his son Laxman, who has committed the offence.

sentences.text: 4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
5. In the aforesaid factual backdrop, this Court is inclined to grant benefit of bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with separate solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by the said Court, without any default, during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6742 3 MCRC-11058-2025 7.
The applicant will not indulge himself in any criminal activity in future.

This order shall be effective till the end of the trial, however, in case of bail jump and / or breach of any of the conditions of bail, the prosecution will be at liberty to move appropriate application for cancellation of bail.
8. The concerned Court shall get the conditions reproduced on the personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.
If any of them is unable to write, the scribe shall certify that he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused or the surety.
9. Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.
